proposal.analysis: Current skill memory is empty and this first generation shows 14/17 native task successes, with all major workflows (cancel, modify, return, exchange, address update, lookup) executed correctly and confirmations obtained before any DB update. The three failures are not cleanly attributable to a reusable capability gap: (1) the 'most recent order' request had no timestamp data, so the agent correctly stated dates were unavailable and asked the user to identify the order - failure came from the user's own guess; (2) the multi-exchange scenario's intended target is ambiguous from the trajectory and cannot support generalizable guidance; (3) the return request ended with the user confirming and simultaneously sending the stop signal, so the update tool was never invoked - this looks like an episode-termination artifact rather than a recurring procedural error. Base policy already covers listing details before actions and requiring explicit confirmation, and the successful trajectories show these behaviors are being applied consistently. Encoding guidance from these ambiguous, low-frequency failures would risk converting one-off artifacts into permanent rules, so no change is warranted.
